newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Former Brazil first lady denies corruption charges.
newsitem.headline: Former Brazil first lady denies corruption charges.

text.p: A former Brazilian first lady appeared in court on Monday and denied allegations that she participated in a scam involving milk money for the poor.

Rosane Collor, wife of ex-president Fernando Collor, denied charges filed by federal prosecutors that in 1991, while head of a poverty-relief organisation, she authorised a purchase of 1.6 million tons of powdered milk at three times market prices.
In a statement read out in a Brasilia courtroom, Collor, 32, also denied prosecution claims that she received payment from companies alleged to have benefited from the purported scam.
Collor, whose husband Fernando Collor resigned as president amid a separate corruption scandal in 1992, had no comment for reporters as she left the court.
Rosane and five other people have been accused of corruption offences that carry jail sentences of between two and 12 years. Her lawyers were due to present further defence arguments later this week.
